title: Antiemetic drug fosaprepitant exerts anti-tumor effects against NSCLC by targeting FAK to inhibit AKT and JNK/c-Jun pathways.
authors: Wang, Ying; Shao, Yu-Na; Ma, Chen-Kang; Shu, Chen-Ying; Zhang, Yi-Hua; Lu, Di; Zhang, Hui-Ling; Zhu, Jian-Jie; Zeng, Yuan-Yuan; Li, Jian-Jun; Yan, Zhao-Wei; Liu, Ze-Yi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究止吐药Fosaprepitant靶向FAK蛋白抑制非小细胞肺癌，属于药物-蛋白互作，与蛋白质-DNA互作及TF-DNA体系无关。
abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is an aggressive malignancy with a poor prognosis. Abnormal expression of focal adhesion kinase (FAK) is closely linked to NSCLC progression, highlighting the need for effective FAK inhibitors in NSCLC treatment. In this study we conducted high-throughput virtual screening combined with cellular assays to identify potential FAK inhibitors for NSCLC treatment. Fosaprepitant (FOS), a clinical antiemetic drug, exhibited a high affinity for FAK with a K(D) value of 4.35 x 10(-)(5) M. The direct interaction between FOS and FAK was confirmed by molecular docking, molecular dynamics, drug affinity responsive target stability and surface plasmon resonance analysis. We showed that FOS (15, 25 muM) dose-dependently inhibited the proliferation, migration and invasion of A549 and H1299 cells by targeting FAK. The IC(50) values in inhibiting the cell viability at 24 h were 73.05 and 126.1 muM, respectively. Knockdown FAK reversed the inhibitory effects of FOS on A549 cells. Using RNA sequencing and Western blotting analysis, we demonstrated that FOS treatment led to downregulation of the AKT and JNK/c-Jun signaling pathways in A549 and H1299 cells. Importantly, point mutation analyses revealed that FOS primarily targeted the Y925 phosphorylation site on FAK. In A549 cells xenograft nude mouse model, administration of FOS (20, 60 mg/kg, i.p. every 2 d for 2 weeks) dose-dependently suppressed the tumor growth. Collectively, FOS exhibits significant anti-NSCLC activity both in vitro and in vivo by binding to FAK and inhibiting its phosphorylation, thereby blocking the AKT and JNK/c-Jun signaling pathways. These results suggest FOS as a novel FAK inhibitor for NSCLC treatment.
abstract_zh: 非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）是一种预后不良的侵袭性恶性肿瘤。局部黏着斑激酶（FAK）的异常表达与NSCLC进展密切相关，凸显了在NSCLC治疗中开发有效FAK抑制剂的需求。在本研究中，我们进行了高通量虚拟筛选结合细胞实验，以识别用于NSCLC治疗的潜在FAK抑制剂。福沙匹坦（FOS），一种临床止吐药物，对FAK表现出高亲和力，其K(D)值为4.35 x 10(-)(5) M。FOS与FAK之间的直接相互作用通过分子对接、分子动力学、药物亲和力响应靶标稳定性及表面等离子体共振分析得到证实。我们表明，FOS（15, 25 μM）通过靶向FAK，剂量依赖性地抑制A549和H1299细胞的增殖、迁移和侵袭。在24小时抑制细胞活力的IC(50)值分别为73.05和126.1 μM。敲低FAK逆转了FOS对A549细胞的抑制作用。通过RNA测序和Western blotting分析，我们证明FOS处理导致A549和H1299细胞中AKT和JNK/c-Jun信号通路的下调。重要的是，点突变分析揭示FOS主要靶向FAK上的Y925磷酸化位点。在A549细胞异种移植裸鼠模型中，给予FOS（20, 60 mg/kg，腹腔注射，每2天一次，持续2周）剂量依赖性地抑制了肿瘤生长。总体而言，FOS通过结合FAK并抑制其磷酸化，从而阻断AKT和JNK/c-Jun信号通路，在体外和体内均表现出显著的抗NSCLC活性。这些结果表明FOS可作为NSCLC治疗的新型FAK抑制剂。
